text:
Aisha (Support): hey team — incoming escalation from AcmeApp, they say generation requests look rate-limited during short bursts even though they’re under their quota. attaching snippet from customer logs.

Aisha (Support): customer reports 2x 2s latency spikes and occasional 429s when they burst ~40 parallel requests for short periods. they’re on hosted API, default quota (60 rps, burst 120).

Aisha (Support): repro steps from customer:
```
for i in {1..40}; do curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-medium","prompt":"summary","max_tokens":60}' &
done
wait
```

Aisha (Support): they also send X-Request-ID headers and see responses like:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 1
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1670000000
```

Jordan (SRE): thanks — can you paste the full raw customer header block? want to confirm they’re hitting the tenant-wide rate limit vs per-route. also, which model variant? rwd-medium as above?

Aisha (Support): pasted in thread DM; they’re using rwd-medium, default region us-west-2. key is a standard free-tier API key (no Dedicated).

Jordan (SRE): preliminary hypothesis: it might be perceived throttling from continuous batching + KV cache lock contention. if a lot of requests share identical prefix tokens, the runtime may serialize KV cache priming or slow down hot-path batching which looks like throttling.

Lee (Runtime Eng): adding context — our continuous batching groups requests into batches up to N tokens or T ms. for short bursts we set max_batch_delay=12ms and batch_size=32 on that SKU. KV cache is per-connection and we do prefix locking to ensure correct KV population; that can induce temporary head-of-line stalls. if many parallel requests are hitting cold KV entries, you can see tail latency and even 429s if upstream admission controllers think the tenant is spiking.

Aisha (Support): ok actionable items? customer wants clear mitigation and repro steps for us to confirm.

Lee (Runtime Eng): steps to reproduce on our side: run their curl loop from a small EC2 in us-west-2 with same key. capture server-side logs for request ids. then reproduce with two variants: (A) default continuous batching + KV enabled; (B) continuous batching but disable prefix KV caching for that route; (C) set max_batch_delay=2ms or increase concurrency per-tenant.

Jordan (SRE): we should also check their token bucket state in tenant metrics at the time — even if nominal quota is 60 rps, burst allowance may be consumed after prior activity. also confirm if they hit per-connection concurrency throttle (we have per-connection streams limits).

Aisha (Support): customer confirmed they were idle for ~10 minutes before the burst. they provided request-ids: rwd-req-0a3c, rwd-req-0a3d, rwd-req-0a3e.

InfraBot: ingestion-log rwd-req-0a3c: assigned to node gw-12; KV-cache: miss -> prime; batch_wait: 10ms; result_code: 200; latency_ms: 480
InfraBot: ingestion-log rwd-req-0a3d: assigned to node gw-12; KV-cache: miss -> prime; batch_wait: 11ms; result_code: 429 (throttled by admission)

Lee (Runtime Eng): that pattern matches KV miss + batching delay then an admission throttle firing mid-burst when too many long-running batches hit GPU allocation simultaneously. node gw-12 may have hit its tenant concurrency cap and started returning 429 from the admission controller.

Jordan (SRE): quick mitigation for customer: 1) suggest reducing client-side parallelism slightly (e.g., from 40 -> 20) to avoid the admission controller spike; 2) if they need same latency at 40 concurrent, recommend upgrading to Dedicated or request a quota bump; 3) short-term, advise adding jitter and a 100-200ms stagger to their burst.

Aisha (Support): any runtime config changes we can do to reduce false throttling without changing customer quota?

Lee (Runtime Eng): we can tune max_batch_delay down for the shared hosted pool (danger: increases ops cost), or implement smarter KV priming (speculative warm on prefix trends). another non-invasive option: for that tenant route we can lower max_batch_delay to 6ms which reduces batch head-of-line holdups, but might increase GPU kernel invocation frequency. we shouldn’t change globally without product sign-off.

Jordan (SRE): action plan:
- Support: ask AcmeApp to apply client jitter and drop concurrency to 20 and confirm behavior (Aisha).
- Runtime Eng: run side-by-side repro under controlled load and capture admission + KV metrics (Lee).
- SRE: check tenant quota history and node gw-12 load around timestamps and see if this is isolated (Jordan).

Aisha (Support): communicated mitigations to customer and asked them to try reduced parallelism + jitter. they also asked for a quick explanation they can pass to their app team — can we include a short note about KV cache/prefixes?

Lee (Runtime Eng): pasteable blurb: "When many near-identical prompts hit the service in a tight burst, the runtime can spend time priming per-connection KV caches and forming batches. If several large batches prime simultaneously, admission controls may throttle to protect overall cluster stability, which looks like transient 429s or latency spikes. To mitigate: stagger requests with jitter, reduce peak parallelism, or use Dedicated capacity for predictable bursts. We can also tune server-side batching parameters or enable speculative KV warming for high-frequency prefixes on request."

Aisha (Support): perfect, I’ll send that. any logs/diagnostics we should attach for the ticket?

Jordan (SRE): include the ingress logs (node assignment + KV hit/miss + batch_wait + admission verdict) and the tenant quota timeline. attach the sample curl loop and our suggested client changes.

Aisha (Support): timeline update for customer: we’ll follow up in 24h after they try the client-side changes; Lee/Jordan will run internal repro and post results here. thanks all :thumbsup:

Lee (Runtime Eng): starting repro run now — I’ll post a short log dump in ~30m.

InfraBot: job repro-1799951234 started on infra-runner-7

Jordan (SRE): noted — if we confirm it’s KV priming contention, we should create a short RFC for speculative KV priming + telemetry exposing per-prefix hotness so customers can opt in.

Aisha (Support): closing loop with customer for now, will reopen thread once we have test results.

Lee (Runtime Eng): repro results (quick): with 40 parallel cold-prefix requests -> 35% 429s within first 5s; with 40 parallel but with 100ms jitter -> 0% 429s, median latency down from 420ms -> 180ms. will dump full trace in separate thread.

Aisha (Support): great, forwarding results to AcmeApp and recommending jitter + consider quota bump or Dedicated if they need sustained high bursts.

Jordan (SRE): filing follow-up ticket for KV priming telemetry: KF-1973.

Aisha (Support): thanks team — marking as triaged.
